questions.stem: What is the primary function of the epidermal cells in the root?
questions.solution: Epidermal cells in the root are primarily responsible for absorbing water and minerals due to their thin cell walls and the presence of root hairs that increase surface area. Photosynthesis occurs in cells with chloroplasts, which are not found in root epidermal cells. Structural support is provided by other root tissues, and food storage is not the main function of these cells.

hi.stem: मूल के एपिडर्मल कोशिकाओं का प्राथमिक कार्य क्या है?
hi.solution: मूल के एपिडर्मल कोशिकाएं अपनी पतली कोशिका भित्ति एवं मूल बालों की उपस्थिति के कारण जल एवं खनिज अवशोषित करने के लिए मुख्य रूप से जिम्मेदार होती हैं। प्रकाश संश्लेषण क्लोरोप्लास्ट वाली कोशिकाओं में होता है, जो मूल एपिडर्मल कोशिकाओं में नहीं पाए जाते। संरचनात्मक समर्थन अन्य मूल ऊतकों द्वारा प्रदान किया जाता है, और भोजन संग्रहण इन कोशिकाओं का मुख्य कार्य नहीं है।

mr.stem: मूळातील एपिडर्मल कोशिकांचा प्राथमिक कार्य काय आहे?

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the endodermis in plant roots?
choices: It has intercellular spaces between its cells
It has a layer of collenchymatous cells
It is made of thick-walled parenchymatous cells
It has a waxy layer called suberin
questions.solution: The endodermis in plant roots has a waxy layer called suberin, which helps regulate water movement into the vascular tissues. Intercellular spaces are not characteristic of the endodermis, as it is a tightly packed layer. Collenchymatous cells are typically found in other parts of the plant, not the endodermis. Thick-walled parenchymatous cells are more associated with other root layers, not the endodermis.

questions.stem: Which part of the stem provides mechanical strength to the young stem?
questions.solution: The hypodermis contains collenchymatous cells that offer structural support and mechanical strength to the young stem. The epidermis is primarily a protective layer and does not provide significant mechanical strength. The cortex is involved in storage and transport, not strength. The endodermis regulates water movement and lacks the structural properties needed for mechanical support.

questions.stem: In a monocot stem, where are the vascular bundles located?
choices: In a ring around the stem
Only near the center of the stem
Only in the outer layers of the stem
questions.solution: In a monocot stem, vascular bundles are scattered throughout the stem rather than arranged in a ring or concentrated in specific areas. This arrangement differs from dicot stems, which typically have vascular bundles in a ring. The other options incorrectly place the bundles in restricted regions, which does not match the actual structure of monocot stems.

questions.stem: What is the main function of the vascular bundles in a leaf?
choices: Provide mechanical support to the leaf
Store food material in the leaf
Transport water and minerals in the leaf
Carry out photosynthesis in the leaf
questions.solution: Vascular bundles are responsible for transporting water and minerals throughout the leaf, which is essential for the plant's survival. Structures like the mesophyll are involved in photosynthesis, while other tissues provide mechanical support or store food. The vascular bundles do not carry out photosynthesis themselves.

questions.stem: If a flower has a tricarpellary syncarpous ovary, which of the following is most likely true?
choices: The flower has three separate carpels
The flower has three fused carpels
questions.solution: The term 'tricarpellary' indicates the presence of three carpels, and 'syncarpous' means those carpels are fused together. Therefore, the flower has three fused carpels. The other options incorrectly suggest a different number of carpels or that they are not fused.

questions.stem: A plant has a leaf with stomata on both surfaces and undifferentiated mesophyll. What type of leaf is it most likely to be?
questions.solution: An isobilateral leaf has stomata on both surfaces and undifferentiated mesophyll, which matches the description. Dorsiventral leaves typically have stomata only on the lower surface and differentiated mesophyll. Monocot leaves usually have a different structure, and dicot leaves generally have a different mesophyll arrangement.

hi.stem: एक पौधे के पत्ते में दोनों सतहों पर स्टोमेटा हैं और मैसोफिल अस्पष्ट है। यह पत्ता सबसे अधिक संभावना किस प्रकार का पत्ता होगा?

questions.stem: Why do monocot roots not undergo secondary growth?

Because they lack a cambium layer
Because they have more xylem bundles
Because they have a sclerenchymatous hypodermis
questions.solution: The correct answer is because they lack a cambium layer, as secondary growth requires a cambium to produce additional vascular tissues. Because monocot roots have more vascular bundles
Because monocot roots have a larger number of xylem bundles
Because monocot roots have a larger number of endodermal cells
